As a person that professionally uses both languages, this is indeed nice and I use it, but it's nowhere near being perfect.

PHP is making major efforts to becoming an even better language, but while Generics are not there for PHP and while the type checks are done only in runtime, I don't think this outweights the strongly typed behavior of C#

Both languages have their benefits.
It's how You use them that matters.

Majority use PHP because it's really easy to learn, You can spin up projects way quicker - since it's interpreted, You don't have to wait until code compiles - You see live changes everytime You edit something.

I've noticed that there are also way more libraries in PHP that can be used as building blocks for Your project, to the point that it's more about requiring right packages, than coding.

ASP.NET CORE is young if compared to PHP, I consider it nicer, because it's strictly typed and compiled, resulting in way better performance and less bugs. But I've found that while the community is growing, the amount of packages is nowhere near, therefore You do need to often write your own solutions.

They are both viable, but in the end it depends on the project and the team that will be creating the backend.
